binders: Positive integer dimensions m and n, with m ≥ n, and a fixed full-column-rank input A ∈ R^{m×n}, written A=(a₁,…,aₙ). [PDF p. 2, printed 300, anchor "opening setup and notation preceding Algorithm 1"]

The computed first-column quantities q₁ ∈ R^m and r₁₁ ∈ R are produced by Algorithm 2, with A₁=(a₁), Q₁=(q₁), and R₁=(r₁₁). [PDF p. 3, printed 301, anchor "Algorithm 2 (CGS-P), first-column initialization"]

For the computed division defining q₁, there exists a perturbation operator G₁ acting on a₁ such that q₁=(I+G₁)a₁/r₁₁ and ‖G₁‖₂≤ε_M. [PDF p. 10, printed 308, anchor "standard-error-bound display immediately before equation (16)"]
hypotheses: Inherited standing assumption: A ∈ R^{m×n}, m ≥ n, and rank(A)=n. [PDF p. 2, printed 300, anchor "opening setup and notation preceding Algorithm 1"]

The arithmetic is IEEE floating-point arithmetic with machine unit ε_M, and the stated relative-error model is restricted to results in the normalized range. [PDF p. 3, printed 301, anchor "floating-point model paragraph following Algorithm 2"]
The first normalization is well-defined because the theorem context makes R nonsingular and hence r₁₁>0. [PDF p. 9, printed 307, anchor "nonsingularity paragraph following equations (14)-(15)"]
conclusions: The computed q₁ admits the exact perturbation representation q₁=(I+G₁)a₁/r₁₁ with ‖G₁‖₂≤ε_M. [PDF p. 10, printed 308, anchor "standard-error-bound display immediately before equation (16)"]
The first-column residual satisfies the complete equality chain A₁−Q₁R₁=a₁−q₁r₁₁=−G₁a₁. [PDF p. 10, printed 308, anchor "residual identity immediately preceding equation (16)"]
Its norm satisfies the complete chain ‖A₁−Q₁R₁‖₂=‖a₁−q₁r₁₁‖₂≤‖G₁‖₂‖a₁‖₂≤ε_M‖a₁‖₂. [PDF p. 10, printed 308, anchor "equation (16)"]
definitions_and_conventions: Aₖ denotes the first k columns of A; therefore A₁ is the one-column matrix (a₁). [PDF p. 4, printed 302, anchor "sentence immediately before Theorem 1"]

Algorithm 2 defines Q₁=(q₁) and R₁=(r₁₁), so Q₁R₁ is identified with the vector q₁r₁₁ in the displayed residual. [PDF p. 3, printed 301, anchor "Algorithm 2 first-column initialization"; PDF p. 10, printed 308, anchor "equation (16)"]

The paper uses unadorned symbols q₁, r₁₁, Q₁, and R₁ for computed quantities; a separate hat notation is not used. [PDF p. 3, printed 301, anchor "Algorithm 2"; PDF p. 4, printed 302, anchor "Theorem 1"]

The identity I and perturbation G₁ must act on R^m because they multiply a₁ ∈ R^m, although their dimensions are not separately declared in the passage. [PDF p. 2, printed 300, anchor "A ∈ R^{m×n} and column notation"; PDF p. 10, printed 308, anchor "q₁=(I+G₁)a₁/r₁₁"]

The products, subtraction, and norm in equation (16) are mathematical post-analysis quantities; the paper does not apply an additional fl operation when evaluating the residual. [PDF p. 10, printed 308, anchor "residual identity and equation (16)"]

statement.algorithm_linkage: The selected result is sourced as the first-column base case for CGS-P, Algorithm 2. Algorithm 1 has the same first-column initialization, so the local algebra of equation (16) is shared, but the enclosing theorem is explicitly about Algorithm 2. Standard error bounds for the componentwise division used to form q₁ are summarized by q₁=(I+G₁)a₁/r₁₁ and ‖G₁‖₂≤ε_M. [PDF p. 10, printed 308, anchor "standard-error-bound display immediately before equation (16)"]

The computed norm satisfies r₁₁=‖a₁‖₂(1+δ₁), |δ₁|≤(0.5m+1)ε_M+O(ε_M²), although this norm-computation error does not appear in the final residual bound because r₁₁ cancels. [PDF p. 9, printed 307, anchor "equation (11)"; PDF p. 10, printed 308, anchor "residual identity"]

The displayed estimate is absolute as written, with scale ‖a₁‖₂; no componentwise residual bound is claimed. [PDF p. 10, printed 308, anchor "equation (16)"]
norms: For vectors, ‖·‖₂ is the Euclidean norm; for matrices such as G₁ and A₁−Q₁R₁, it is the induced spectral 2-norm under the paper's standard numerical-linear-algebra convention. [PDF p. 4, printed 302, anchor "κ₂(Rₖ)=‖Rₖ‖₂‖Rₖ⁻¹‖₂"; PDF p. 10, printed 308, anchor "equation (16)"]
Because A₁−Q₁R₁ has one column, its matrix 2-norm equals the Euclidean norm of a₁−q₁r₁₁, as explicitly written in equation (16). [PDF p. 10, printed 308, anchor "equation (16)"]
The first inequality in equation (16) is the operator-norm action bound ‖G₁a₁‖₂≤‖G₁‖₂‖a₁‖₂. [PDF p. 10, printed 308, anchor "residual identity and equation (16)"]
constants_and_indexing: The selected passage is specifically the k=1 case, with no shifted index or sum over columns. [PDF p. 10, printed 308, anchor "first consider k=1" and "equation (16)"]

contract_plain_english: For the first column of the computed CGS-P factorization, standard floating-point division error can be represented by some operator G₁ with ‖G₁‖₂≤ε_M such that q₁=(I+G₁)a₁/r₁₁. [PDF p. 10, printed 308, anchor "standard-error-bound display immediately before equation (16)"] Consequently, when the computed factors are multiplied and subtracted in exact analysis, A₁−Q₁R₁=a₁−q₁r₁₁=−G₁a₁, and therefore ‖A₁−Q₁R₁‖₂=‖a₁−q₁r₁₁‖₂≤‖G₁‖₂‖a₁‖₂≤ε_M‖a₁‖₂. [PDF p. 10, printed 308, anchor "residual identity and equation (16)"] This is the k=1 base case of Theorem 1's factorization-residual bound, under the standing full-rank, Algorithm 2, normalized-range floating-point, and nonsingularity context. [PDF p. 2, printed 300, anchor "opening setup"; PDF p. 4, printed 302, anchor "Theorem 1"; PDF p. 9, printed 307, anchor "nonsingularity paragraph"]
